Notes: Audited 2026-08-24: the 3150-line implementation with 17 pre-existing passing tests was **not** stale-but-fine as the blank CSV status suggested. Mechanical name-set diff of every function/type in ``libcxx/include/linalg`` against ``[linalg.syn]`` on eel.is found the declared API surface complete (the one apparent miss, ``triangular_matrix_vector_2x2_product``, is a worked example inside a Note, not a real overload). Added the 11 ``[linalg.helpers.concepts]`` exposition-only concepts and retrofitted trailing ``requires``-clauses across ~90 function definitions (BLAS 1 through BLAS 3), landed in 6 commits, each verified against the full ``linalg/`` suite. Deliberately left ``copy``/``scale``/``add``/``swap_elements`` unconstrained: the standard's ``in-object``/``out-object`` concepts exclude rank-0 mdspans, but this fork's ``copy()``/``add()`` (and by the same shape ``scale()``/``swap_elements()``) intentionally and testedly accept rank 0 too (``execution_policies.pass.cpp``'s ``test_add_ranks()``) -- applying the literal concept would regress that. ``|Partial|`` (not ``|Complete|``): the live draft's ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` value is ``202511L``, not this fork's ``202311L``. P3222R0 is the one unresolved link: it is genuinely blocked on P2642R6/``std::constant_wrapper``, same as mdspan ``submdspan``/padded layouts (see ``docs/CXX26_GAPS.md``'s mdspan sub-plan) -- so the FTM cannot honestly advance past ``202311L`` until that chain unblocks, independent of how complete P1673R13's own implementation is. (A full member-by-member prose audit of every function's Preconditions/Effects/Complexity against the standard wording was also not undertaken this session -- ~90 functions; the 17 pre-existing tests, the mechanical name-set diff, a SFINAE-discrimination test (``helper_concepts.pass.cpp``), and P3371R5's real-if-needed fix are real evidence of correctness but not an exhaustive audit. This is an unverified area, not a known defect, and isn't why the status is ``|Partial|`` -- the FTM/P3222R0 blocker above is.) See ``docs/CXX26_GAPS.md`` Tier 3 for the full writeup.

Notes: Not in this CSV at all until 2026-08-24: found by tracing the live draft's ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` value (``202511L``) back through ``cplusplus/draft`` commit history to identify what it actually requires, rather than leaving the gap between it and this fork's ``202311L`` unverified (see P1673R13's row). Of its four required changes: (1) updating (E-taking) overloads for every rank-1/2/k/2k update, (2) overwriting-not-accumulating semantics for the alpha-only overloads, and (4) alpha-only overloads plus the ``scalar``-excludes-mdspan/execution_policy constraint were already present/correct in this fork before this session (predating the P1673R13 SFINAE-retrofit work). (3) was genuinely missing: ``hermitian_matrix_rank_1_update`` and ``hermitian_matrix_rank_k_update`` used ``alpha`` directly instead of ``real-if-needed(alpha)``, and all four ``hermitian_matrix_rank_{1,2,k,2k}_update`` E-taking overloads used ``E[i, i]`` directly instead of ``real-if-needed(E[i, i])`` on the diagonal -- both meant a complex ``alpha`` or a not-quite-Hermitian ``E`` diagonal could leave a nonzero imaginary part on the result's diagonal, which is required to stay real for a Hermitian matrix. Fixed in ``libcxx/include/linalg``; added ``hermitian_real_if_needed.pass.cpp`` with inputs whose ``alpha``/``E`` diagonal have deliberately nonzero imaginary parts (the pre-existing ``rank_updates.pass.cpp`` inputs were all already real there, so the bug was untested). Item (2) (overwriting-not-accumulating) was subsequently verified by reading, not just checking, every non-E overload's body across symmetric/hermitian rank-1/2/k/2k -- all confirmed correct. Post-fix review also found the same diagnostic-omitted-real-if-needed bug is not specific to the rank-update family's ``E`` parameter: ``[linalg.general]`` paragraph 4 states the identical diagonal rule generally, for any function reading through a triangle-tagged, ``hermitian``-named matrix parameter. That covers ``hermitian_matrix_vector_product`` and all four ``hermitian_matrix_product``/``[linalg.algs.blas3.xxmm]`` overloads (whichever argument is the Hermitian factor), which had the identical unfixed stored-vs-conjugated-vs-diagonal branch. Fixed those 6 call sites too, with 3 more test cases (one per distinct index-pair shape: the vector case and both matrix-product factor orderings) verified against a scratch binary before being added to the lit test. Does not by itself unblock the ``__cpp_lib_linalg`` FTM bump to ``202511L`` -- P3222R0 (also in this CSV, still blank status) is earlier in the same chain and remains genuinely blocked on P2642R6/``std::constant_wrapper``; see docs/CXX26_GAPS.md's mdspan sub-plan.
